The '''9th Critics' Choice Awards''' were presented on January 10, 2004, honoring the finest achievements of [[2003 in film|2003 filmmaking]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.today.com/popculture/rings-sweeps-big-prizes-critics-choice-wbna3931892 |title='Rings' sweeps big prizes at Critics' Choice |work=[[Today (American TV program)|Today]] |date=January 11, 2004 |access-date=January 11, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eonline.com/amp/news/46601/critics-choice-hails-king |title=Critics' Choice Hails "King" |first=Joal |last=Ryan |work=[[E!#E! Online|E! Online]] |date=January 11, 2004 |access-date=January 11, 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-jan-13-et-critics13-story.html |title='Rings' cycle continues with four Critics' Choice |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 13, 2004 |access-date=January 13, 2004}}</ref>

==Top 10 films==
(in alphabetical order)

* ''[[Big Fish]]''
* ''[[Cold Mountain (film)|Cold Mountain]]''
* ''[[Finding Nemo]]''
* ''[[In America (film)|In America]]''
* ''[[The Last Samurai]]''
* ''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King]]''
* ''[[Lost in Translation (film)|Lost in Translation]]''
* ''[[Master and Commander: The Far Side of the World]]''
* ''[[Mystic River (film)|Mystic River]]''
* ''[[Seabiscuit (film)|Seabiscuit]]''
